verdict.rationale: Gitleaks documents its own configuration format for writing custom secret-detection rules. It supports composite rules (a primary rule plus required auxiliary rules) and per-rule allowlists, and a repo-level gitleaks.toml or GITLEAKS_CONFIG path is picked up automatically, so organization-specific token formats can be defined and enforced. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of rule fields (regex, entropy, keywords) for matching internal token formats, and independent or hands-on corroboration of custom rules working in practice.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can define custom detection rules for my organization's internal token and secret formats

citations.quote: Gitleaks offers a configuration format you can follow to write your own secret detection rules
In v8.28.0 Gitleaks introduced composite rules, which are made up of a single "primary" rule and one or more auxiliary or `required` rules.
You can define multiple allowlists for a rule to reduce false positives.
You can use `GITLEAKS_CONFIG` to explicitly set a config path _or_ create a `gitleaks.toml` at the root of the repo which will be automatically detected and used by **gitleaks-action**.
